name: Tokyo Dome Natural Hot Springs Spa LaQua
name_ja: 東京ドーム天然温泉 Spa LaQua
about: Spa LaQua is a hot-spring complex on the 5th to 7th floors of the LaQua building in Tokyo Dome City. Its baths use spring water pumped from deep underground, and the facility also has saunas, a relaxation area and massage services. It is open overnight, with the last entry at 8:00 the next morning. Visitors with tattoos or other skin art may not enter, according to GO TOKYO. Children aged 0 to 5 are not admitted.
hours: 11:00-9:00 the next morning (bathing until 8:30; last admission 8:00)
closed: Open daily (may close temporarily for maintenance)
price: Adults 3,500-4,700 yen depending on the day (night admission after 19:00 from 2,500 yen); ages 6-17 from 2,300 yen
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Thermae-Yu
name_ja: テルマー湯 新宿歌舞伎町
about: Thermae-Yu is a 24-hour hot-spring and sauna complex in Kabukicho, a short walk from Shinjuku-sanchome Station. The baths use natural hot-spring water and the facility has several saunas and relaxation areas. The official site says it is open around the clock all year, with bath cleaning from 3:00 to 6:00. A Japan travel directory states that tattoos are accepted only for inbound foreign visitors; check the facility's usage rules before you go.
price: Mon-Thu 3,100 yen; Fri-Sun, holidays and peak days 3,200 yen; extra charge from midnight to 6:00
station: Shinjuku-sanchome Station (Marunouchi Line, Fukutoshin Line, Toei Shinjuku Line)
parking: Paid parking available (about 1,000 yen for up to 6 hours, per the official site banner)

name: Keio Takaosan Onsen Gokurakuyu
name_ja: 京王高尾山温泉 極楽湯
about: This hot-spring facility stands right next to Takaosanguchi Station, at the foot of Mt. Takao, and many hikers stop here after a walk. It has indoor and outdoor baths and saunas, and a massage service is available. Direct trains from Shinjuku reach the station. The official page says it may close temporarily for inspections. Ask the facility about its tattoo policy before visiting.
closed: Open year round (may close temporarily for inspections)
price: Adults about 1,100 yen (varies by season and time)
car: Possible, but the train from Shinjuku is easier

name: Toshimaen Niwa no Yu
about: Niwa no Yu is a day spa beside Toshimaen Station in Nerima. Its hot-spring water comes from about 1,445 metres underground, and the baths face a Japanese garden. There are open-air baths, several saunas, and a swimwear area with an outdoor whirlpool and an outdoor Finnish sauna. The official site says people with tattoos on any part of the body are not allowed in.
price: Weekdays 2,600 yen; weekends and holidays 3,300 yen; peak days 3,400 yen. Ages 13 and over only
station: Toshimaen Station (Seibu Toshima Line, Toei Oedo Line)
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Tokyo Somei Onsen SAKURA
about: Tokyo Somei Onsen SAKURA is a hot-spring facility in Komagome, near Sugamo Station. It has indoor and outdoor baths and a sauna, and towels are rental only. A travel directory lists tattoos, including small ones and tattoo stickers, as not allowed. Overnight stays are not permitted. Children under 6 cannot use the bathing area.
price: Adults 2,100 yen on weekdays, 2,900 yen on weekends, holidays and specific days; ages 6 to elementary school 1,200 yen
station: Sugamo Station (Toei Mita Line, JR Yamanote Line)
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Koganeyu
about: Koganeyu is a renovated neighbourhood sento (public bathhouse) in a residential area of Sumida, about a 6-minute walk from Kinshicho Station. It has a hot-spring bath and an optional sauna, and the sauna add-on is charged separately. The facility's FAQ says guests with tattoos are allowed. Payment is by cash or PayPay only. A second branch opened in Shinjuku in 2026.
price: Adults 600 yen (90 minutes); junior high 500 yen; elementary 200 yen; infants 100 yen
station: Kinshicho Station (JR Chuo-Sobu Line, Hanzomon Line)

name: Takara-yu
about: Takara-yu is a traditional neighbourhood sento in Adachi with a classic temple-style building and a garden. Entry is the standard Tokyo sento fare, 600 yen for adults since August 2026. It is a long walk from Kita-Senju Station, so some visitors take a bus. Ask the bathhouse about its tattoo policy.
price: Adults 600 yen, elementary school 200 yen, under 6 100 yen
station: Kita-Senju Station (JR Joban Line, Hibiya Line, Chiyoda Line, Tobu Skytree Line, Tsukuba Express)

name: Oshiage Onsen Daikokuyu
about: Daikokuyu is a neighbourhood public bathhouse (sento) in Sumida Ward, a short walk from Tokyo Skytree. The building has a traditional tiled roof, and the baths use dark, naturally sourced hot spring water. Saunas are available for a small extra fee. The bathhouse stays open until 10:00 the next morning, so it suits late evenings.
hours: Weekdays 15:00-10:00 (next morning); Saturdays from 14:00; Sundays and holidays from 13:00
closed: Tuesdays (Wednesday if Tuesday is a public holiday)
price: Adults 600 yen, junior high 500 yen, elementary 200 yen, infants 100 yen; sauna extra (about 300-400 yen)
station: Oshiage Station (Hanzomon Line, Asakusa Line, Keisei Oshiage Line, Tobu Skytree Line)
car: Not recommended; public transport is easier

name: Jindaiji Onsen Yumori no Sato
name_ja: 深大寺天然温泉 湯守の里
about: Yumori no Sato is a day-use hot spring facility in Chofu, close to Jindaiji Temple and the Jindaiji soba area. It offers indoor and outdoor baths with natural hot spring water, plus extras such as a rock bath and massage. Guests with tattoos may enter only if the tattoos can be covered with stickers or similar, according to the official FAQ. A free shuttle bus runs from Chofu Station and Musashi-Sakai Station.
closed: Open year-round (temporary closures for maintenance possible)
price: Weekdays: adults 1,080 yen, children 650 yen; weekends, holidays and peak periods: adults 1,180 yen, children 750 yen; extras cost more
station: Chofu Station (Keio Line); free shuttle bus about 8 minutes, also from Musashi-Sakai Station (JR Chuo Line)
car: Possible, with on-site parking; the lot can fill up on busy days

name: Saya no Yudokoro (Maenohara Onsen)
name_ja: 前野原温泉 さやの湯処
about: Saya no Yudokoro is a large bathhouse in Itabashi Ward built around Maenohara Onsen hot spring water. It has a range of baths, a rock-bed sauna for an extra fee and private baths that can be booked by the hour. It is open every day until midnight. Guests with tattoos can enter if they fully cover them with up to two cover stickers provided by the facility.
closed: No regular closing days (occasional closure for maintenance)
price: Adults 970 yen (1,300 yen on weekends and holidays), children 600 yen (900 yen on weekends and holidays); towel and lounge wear rental 380 yen each
